column3: The Hebrew has an active plural subject refining gold; BSB uses a passive.
The Hebrew names dust and stone; BSB says earth and ore.
The Hebrew leaves the subject unnamed; BSB explicitly supplies man.
The Hebrew shifts to plural subjects for hanging and swaying; BSB continues with he.
The Hebrew says like fire without the added as by in BSB.
The Hebrew names gold dust with a masculine possessor; BSB describes the rocks containing flecks of gold.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew pictures sons of pride; BSB says proud beasts.
The Hebrew leaves the subject unnamed and pictures stretching out his hand; BSB supplies the miner and says strikes.
The Hebrew has eye in the singular and completed actions; BSB has eyes and present verbs.
The Hebrew names restraining streams from dripping; BSB says stopping up their sources.
The Hebrew asks for the place of understanding; BSB asks where it dwells.

The Hebrew uses completed verbs of saying; BSB uses present verbs.
